lens: Adversarial critique — over-engineering / simpler-path. Judged against the 7 target requirements and the confirmed game seam (PHASE0-FINDINGS.md, decompiled BigAmbitions).
verdict: Needs trimming. The core call (D9 Option B: mod-owned plan + reuse ba:skill_logisticsmanager) is right and well-argued. But the plan then re-adds most of the cost it just saved: a Harmony-injected BizMan tab, a Phase-3 custom skill, a dual persistence sink with grace-day state machines, contract-snapshot restore, ScheduleAutoFiller for store rosters, and a MistakeModel subsystem. Requirements 2/3/4 are already delivered for free by vanilla UI the moment you reuse the real skill — the plan doesn't fully cash that in and keeps building office-parity UI on top. Cut ~60% of the surface and the user barely notices.
topIssues: The 'mirror the HQ manager-plan system' framing IS the over-engineering. Reusing ba:skill_logisticsmanager already routes hiring through the vanilla Recruitment Agency, puts the manager in My Employees with a real wage, and makes them schedulable on the HQ desk via the vanilla Schedule tab — requirements 2, 3 and 4 satisfied with ZERO mod UI. The only gap is the job-title label reading 'Logistics Manager'. The plan acknowledges this (D9/D10) then still specs a custom Recruit button and a full custom 'Store Managers' BizMan tab to re-create a flow the game already gives you.

The Harmony BizMan tab (Phase 2) is the highest-risk, lowest-value item. Decomp confirms HQ tabs are hardcoded, name-matched prefab children ('PricingManagers','LogisticsManagers','HRManagers'...) in HeadquartersList/BizManBusiness with a private _tabs list and private SetTab/SetUpTabs — a new tab needs prefab surgery PLUS Harmony on 3 private members PLUS a DegradedToPanel fallback you have to build and maintain anyway. Payoff: the limits panel opens as a BizMan tab instead of Options>Mods. Since hiring and scheduling are ALREADY in the office/vanilla UI, the player will barely register that the store-list config lives one menu away.

The Phase-3 custom skill (storemanager:skill_manager) should be cut permanently, not deferred. Research flags ~8 unguarded SkillHelper.GetData(name).<field> NPE sites, no persistence of mod skills across reloads (re-inject every city load AND scene reload), a Unity-authored SkillData asset + 28px icon + gradient on the exact engine version, and a Harmony finalizer guard — all so the title says 'Store Manager'. Enormous risk surface for a cosmetic label.

Persistence is over-built. GameInstance.modData exists (Dictionary<string,string>, GameInstance.cs:248) and travels with the save — that alone is enough. The plan adds: an OdinSerializer JSON envelope (it's a string dict — plain JSON is fine), a second persistentDataPath file sink 'wired from day one', save-identity keying, a 3-day grace-day counter + dormant state machine, revive-only-if-employee-resolves, and per-assignment DeliveryContract snapshot capture/restore-on-detach mirroring PricingManagerPlan.originalStorePrices.

MistakeModel / ManagementSkill 1-5 / ManagerRank ladder are now vestigial and still in the plan. With a real EmployeeInstance carrying a real 0-100 skill and a real wage, the bespoke competence model, deterministic daily mistake roll, 4-rank wage table and DifficultyProfile coupling lose their anchor. 'Manager sometimes makes mistakes' is invisible flavor that can't be tuned without playtest — it shouldn't gate v1.

ScheduleAutoFiller for the supervised-store rosters (requirement 7 'day-to-day') is a Google OR-Tools CP-SAT solve on a background thread kicked from onNewDay, racing the game's own scheduling and delivery passes. Restock via DeliveryContract is the headline of requirement 7; roster auto-fill is a second, independently risky integration bolted into the same tick.

Phase 1 is not a minimal v1 — it's 14 rewrite/add tasks including a new Feedback interop, new DeliveryContracts interop, new Recruiting interop, ManagerDirectory rewrite, DailyOperations rewrite, onJobChange reconcile, grace windows, and modData+fallback plumbing. There's no genuinely small first milestone that proves the restock loop is fun before the scaffolding is built.
recommendedChanges: Cash in the free wins and stop there for hiring/scheduling. v1 instruction to the player: 'Recruit a Logistics Manager from the Recruitment Agency, hire them, assign to your HQ, and put them on the HQ desk in the Schedule tab.' No mod hire UI, no Recruit button. The mod only needs a read: EmployeeHelper.GetEmployeeInstances(withAssignedAddress=HQ, withSkills=[ba:skill_logisticsmanager]) filtered by IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift().

Cut the Harmony BizMan tab entirely (not defer). Ship the assign/limits UI as ONE ModOptions panel: a dropdown of eligible scheduled managers, a multi-toggle list of player-owned retail stores (capped at 1 + floor(skill/25)), and per-selected-store sliders for restock budget cap + target days-of-stock + staffing level. If ModOptions primitives can't do per-store rows, use a single ModOption.SpawnUi panel with a store-picker that rebinds the sliders — still no Harmony, no prefab work.

Cut the custom skill permanently. Reuse ba:skill_logisticsmanager. Add a one-line guard: if LogisticsManagerHelper.GetAssignedPlanForEmployee(id) != null, refuse to adopt them and show a warning line in the panel. If thematic overlap with restocking bothers the user, use ba:skill_hrmanager instead. Decide now.

Collapse persistence to: one modData key, plain JSON (Newtonsoft, already a game dep) of List<StoreManagerPlan>. Write on GlobalEvents.onSaveGame, read on [ModEntryOnCityLoad]. On load, for each plan, if GetEmployeeById fails -> disable that plan's repeating contracts and drop the plan. No fallback file, no OdinSerializer envelope, no grace-day counter, no snapshot/restore — on detach just set the repeating DeliveryContract enabled=false and notify.

Cut MistakeModel, ManagementSkill 1-5 bucketing, ManagerRank ladder and DifficultyProfile coupling from v1. The manager does the job competently; skill only scales MaxStores and (optionally) restock target precision. Re-introduce imperfection later once the loop is proven fun in playtest.

Cut ScheduleAutoFiller / roster top-up and complaint/leave/training handling from v1. Requirement 7's headline is 'stocked via delivery' — deliver exactly that. Day-to-day roster and HR are a separate, later slice.
Keep the console commands (already built) as the power-user + test surface. They de-risk the whole thing without any UI investment.

Reuse the exact vanilla feedback idiom: Contact.EnsurePermanentContact('storemanager_alerts', ContactCategoryName.ImportsAndGoods, ...) for the weekly digest (this is literally what LogisticsManagerPlan does, LogisticsManagerPlan.cs:44) + Notifications.Show toasts per order/cap-hit. No new phone app — that was correctly excluded already; keep it excluded.
v1ScopeRecommendation: Minimal v1 (no Harmony, no bundle, no custom skill, no new domain subsystems): (1) Player recruits+hires+schedules a Logistics Manager entirely through vanilla UI — requirements 2/3/4 done for free. (2) One ModOptions/SpawnUi panel: pick the scheduled manager, toggle up to 1+floor(skill/25) owned retail stores, set per-store restock budget cap + target days-of-stock + staffing level (global defaults seed new picks) — requirements 5/6. (3) GlobalEvents.onNewDay handler: for each assigned store, get-or-create its DeliveryContract, set enabled+repeatingOrder, tune item amounts toward target within the weekly budget cap (per-store WeekTally), guarded by DeliveryHelper.CanModifyContract; toast on order placed / cap hit — requirement 7. (4) Weekly Contact-thread digest + per-action toasts — requirement 1. (5) Persist List<StoreManagerPlan> as plain JSON in GameInstance.modData['StoreManager.plans.v1']; on load drop plans whose manager is gone and disable their contracts. (6) Console commands as the test/power surface. Everything else — BizMan tab, custom skill, MistakeModel, ScheduleAutoFiller, training/leave/complaints, contract snapshot/restore, grace windows, fallback file sink, player self-scheduling/register-handoff — is post-v1 and most of it is never worth it.
mustVerifyInGameFirst: Can a Logistics Manager employee be assigned to an HQ address and given an HQ-desk WorkShift WITHOUT the game auto-creating a LogisticsManagerPlan? (If assigning via the vanilla LogisticsManagers HQ tab always makes a plan, the mod must steer players to the Recruitment Agency path instead and detect/refuse plan-bound employees.)

Is DeliveryHelper.CanModifyContract(day) true at the point GlobalEvents.onNewDay fires, and do mod edits to DeliveryContractItem.amount survive the game's own BusinessHelper.HandleWholesaleDeliveries pass on the same day? Test against an existing player-created contract before creating any from scratch.
Creating a DeliveryContract from nothing: is choosing wholesaleAddress safe/unambiguous, and does an invalid choice fail silently (no delivery) vs throw?

Does GameInstance.modData actually round-trip through BOTH save paths (Newtonsoft TypeNameHandling.Auto and the OdinSerializer binary path) for a multi-hundred-char string value? Confirmed the field exists (GameInstance.cs:248); the round-trip is unverified.

Does an HQ reliably contain an office-desk workstation whose suitableSkills includes ba:skill_logisticsmanager, so the manager can actually be scheduled? Panel must detect absence and tell the player.
GlobalEvents.onJobChange coverage: does it fire on fired / quit / poached, so the per-day reconcile isn't the only safety net?
